number_of_offences: Number of offences/counts charged: Not stated; Number of offences finally upheld: Not stated
key_evidence_accepted: The High Court accepted that the appellant was found in the deceased's house on the fateful day, his fingerprint was found on a plastic cover, his clothes were blood-stained and matched the blood group of the deceased, the ornaments of the deceased were recovered from the appellant, and the weapon of offence was discovered at the instance of the appellant.
witness_credibility: The court assessed that the witnesses PW-6 and PW-7 saw the appellant briefly and identified him after a long lapse of time, but the circumstances of their identification were not satisfactory. The court also noted that the witnesses did not provide any identifying details about the deceased's relatives.
trial_duration: Dates of offence: 5th November, 1990; Trial judgment: Not stated; High Court decision: Conviction on circumstantial evidence; Supreme Court decision: Acquittal
legal_representation: Counsel for the accused: Not stated; Counsel for the State: Not stated
investigation_status: FIR registered, charge sheet filed, trial completed
procedural_irregularity: The investigation was not fair; no Test Identification Parade was held; the fingerprint identification was shrouded in mystery; blood-stained crowbar not sent for chemical examination
appeal_history: Trial court: Acquittal; High Court: Conviction; Supreme Court: Appeal allowed, conviction set aside, acquittal confirmed
prosecution_argument: The prosecution argued that the appellant went to the house of the victim-deceased and robbed her ornaments and murdered her. The High Court relied on the circumstances that the appellant was found in the deceased's house on the fateful day, his fingerprint was found on a plastic cover, his clothes were blood-stained and matched the blood group of the deceased, the ornaments of the deceased were recovered at the instance of the appellant, and the weapon of offence was discovered at the instance of the appellant.
defence_argument: The defence argued that the High Court's reliance on probabilities was insufficient, as there was no evidence about the appellant's whereabouts from 1 P.M. to 8.30 P.M., no TIP was held, and the fingerprint identification was shrouded in mystery. The trial court's acquittal was a plausible view and the High Court should not have upset it.
legal_principle_applied: In a case of circumstantial evidence, there has to be some degree of trustworthiness and certainty about the existence of the circumstances; mere probabilities are certainly not enough.
